title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student finishes machine training in a chat on Monday. On Thursday she opens a brand-new session. Your assistant has the agent loop and tools, but no saved notes. What does it know about Monday?

options.text: Everything, because the model keeps its own memory of past chats
A summary, which the model writes itself when each chat ends
Nothing, because each new session starts with an empty context
Only the last message, because the window keeps one final turn

items.stem: Your assistant's fixed part (system prompt, tool descriptions and the question) is 1,500 tokens. It calls the model, requests one tool that returns 2,000 tokens, calls the model again, requests a second tool that returns 500 tokens, and calls the model a third time for the final answer. Ignore the model's own short requests and its output. What is the total number of input tokens processed over all three calls?
Your team has 40 machine manuals totalling about 2 million tokens, and a student asks about one setting on one machine. Which design best fits a small model budget?

options.text: Index the manuals and give the model a search tool that returns a few chunks
Paste all the manuals into the prompt, since larger windows can hold them
Paste the manuals in once, then rely on the model to remember them
Fine-tune the model on the manuals so that no search is needed

items.stem: In one or two sentences: why should the assistant save a student's training status in a file or database instead of just leaving it in the conversation history?
Students often search your manuals for exact error codes such as "E-417". The embedding search sometimes returns chunks about similar codes instead. What is the best fix?

options.text: Switch off retrieval, so that the model answers from its own knowledge
Use only embedding search, since it finds meaning better than keywords
Return many more chunks, so that the right one is always included
Add keyword search, such as BM25, and combine it with embeddings
